questions.q: What is the core trade-off between online and offline migration, per this lesson?
options: Offline is simpler but risks a longer downtime window; online shrinks downtime to minutes but adds real complexity in monitoring an ongoing sync
Online migration always costs more money with no other differences
Offline migration is impossible for any database larger than 1 GB
There is no real difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: They trade complexity for downtime in opposite directions — neither is universally better.

questions.q: What happens during an online migration between the initial copy and the final cutover?
options: The source stays live and serving traffic while ongoing changes keep syncing to the target
The source database is taken offline immediately and stays offline for the entire migration
Nothing — online migration has no syncing step at all
The target database is deleted and recreated repeatedly until cutover
questions.explain: Online migration's defining feature is that the source keeps serving traffic while changes sync, until a short final cutover.

questions.q: Which three factors does this lesson say actually decide between online and offline migration?
options: Database size and change rate, the business's downtime budget, and the team's readiness to monitor a live sync
The DBA's personal preference, the day of the week, and the weather
Only the total dollar cost of Azure compute
Only whether the database uses Always Encrypted
questions.explain: These three — technical (size/change rate), business (downtime budget), and operational (monitoring readiness) — are the real deciding factors.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe the choice as something a DBA "presents to the business" rather than a purely technical decision?
options: Because the real choice is about which risk (downtime vs. migration complexity) the business is willing to accept, not just a technical preference
Because the business always makes the final technical decision regardless of DBA input
Because online migration is illegal without executive sign-off
Because offline migration requires no DBA involvement at all
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as presenting a real cost/risk trade-off, not defaulting to one option without asking what the business actually needs.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what mistake does a DBA make by defaulting to online migration for every database?
options: Adding real complexity and a monitoring burden for a benefit the business may not have actually needed
Making the migration completely impossible to perform
Guaranteeing zero downtime in every single case with no exceptions
Eliminating the need for any assessment step beforehand
questions.explain: Online migration's complexity is only worth it when the downtime savings actually matter to the business — defaulting to it without asking wastes that cost.
